```{r}
#| label: setup
#| output: false

# Load packages
pacman::p_load(here, httr2, leaflet, sf, scales, tidyverse)
```

```{r}
#| label: download-data
#| output: false

# Download original crime and population data into the workspace
request(
  "https://mpjashby.github.io/crimemappingdata/japan_violence_counts.rds"
) |>
  req_perform(path = here("data", "raw", "japan_violence_counts.rds"))

# Download original prefecture boundaries into the workspace
request("https://mpjashby.github.io/crimemappingdata/japan_prefectures.gpkg") |>
  req_perform(path = here("data", "raw", "japan_prefectures.gpkg"))
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| output: false

# Read crime and population data, removing the repeated prefix from measure
# names
violence <- here("data", "raw", "japan_violence_counts.rds") |>
  read_rds() |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(measure = str_remove(measure, "number of "))

# Read prefecture boundaries as spatial data, then transform to use longitude
# and latitude
prefectures <- here("data", "raw", "japan_prefectures.gpkg") |>
  read_sf() |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  st_transform("EPSG:4326")
```

```{r}
#| label: calculate-rates
#| output: false

# Extract population from the raw data
prefecture_pop <- violence |>
  filter(measure == "population (thousands)") |>
  # Keep only the prefecture names and the population value, but change the name
  # to `pop` since `value` is ambiguous
  select(prefecture, pop = value) |>
  # Convert the population measure to number of people, since in the raw data it
  # is in thousands
  mutate(pop = pop * 1000)

# Extract violence counts from the raw data
violence_counts <- violence |>
  filter(measure %in% c("violent crimes", "homicides", "robberies", "rapes")) |>
  # Rename the ambiguous `measure` and `value` columns
  rename(crime_type = measure, crimes = value)

# Join the data then calculate crime rates and ranks
violence_rates <- prefectures |>
  # Select only the columns from the prefecture boundary data that we need, and
  # rename the column containing the English name for each prefecture
  select(prefecture = adm1_en, geom) |>
  # Join violence counts to prefecture boundaries
  left_join(violence_counts, by = join_by(prefecture == prefecture)) |>
  # Join population counts
  left_join(prefecture_pop, by = join_by(prefecture == prefecture)) |>
  # Calculate an incidence rate
  mutate(rate = crimes / pop * 100000) |>
  # Rank each prefecture for each type of crime (note that `.by = crime_type`
  # means the ranks are calculated separately for each crime type)
  mutate(rank = min_rank(desc(rate)), .by = crime_type) |>
  mutate(
    # Create a label describing the rate in each prefecture to be used in the
    # report *text*
    label = str_glue(
      "{prefecture} ({number(rate, accuracy = 0.1)} per 100,000)"
    ),
    # Create a label to be used in the *maps*
    map_label = str_glue(
      "{prefecture}: {number(rate, accuracy = 0.1)} {crime_type} per 100,000 ",
      "residents (rank {ordinal(rank)} of {nrow(prefectures)})"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: summary-statistics
#| output: false

# Calculate national rates from total counts and total population
national_rates <- violence_rates |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  summarise(rate = sum(crimes) / sum(pop) * 100000, .by = crime_type)

# Extract the five highest rates of overall violence into a vector in descending
# order, including any ties
high_five <- violence_rates |>
  # Keep only the overall violence rates
  filter(crime_type == "violent crimes") |>
  # Keep just the five prefectures with the highest rates
  slice_max(order_by = rate, n = 5) |>
  # Extract the labels into a vector that we can include in the report text
  pull("label")

# Select the highest and lowest rate prefecture for each individual crime type
highest <- violence_rates |>
  slice_max(order_by = rate, n = 1, by = crime_type)
lowest <- violence_rates |>
  slice_min(order_by = rate, n = 1, by = crime_type)
```

The Statistics Bureau of Japan supplies crime counts for Japan's `r nrow(prefectures)` prefectures. This report describes regional variation in recorded violent crime in 2012. It covers overall violent crime and separately homicides, robberies and rapes.


## Overall violent crime

The national rate of overall violent crime was `r number(pull(filter(national_rates, crime_type == "violent crimes"), "rate"), accuracy = 0.1)` recorded violent crimes per 100,000 residents. The five prefectures with the highest rates were `r high_five`, while the lowest was in `r pull(filter(lowest, crime_type == "violent crimes"), "label")`. @fig-overall-violence shows the distribution across all prefectures. Select a prefecture to read its rate, or move the pointer over it to show its label.

```{r}
#| label: fig-overall-violence
#| fig-cap: "Overall recorded violent crime per 100,000 residents in Japanese prefectures, 2012"
#| out-width: "100%"

# Extract just the overall violence rates
overall_rates <- filter(violence_rates, crime_type == "violent crimes")

# Create a sequential palette with a fixed domain for this crime rate
overall_colours <- colorNumeric(
  palette = "Reds",
  domain = pull(overall_rates, "rate")
)

# Create the interactive map
leaflet(overall_rates) |>
  # Add a light base map
  addProviderTiles(
    "OpenStreetMap.Mapnik",
    options = providerTileOptions(opacity = 0.4)
  ) |>
  # Colour prefectures by rate, with labels and click-to-open popups
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~ overall_colours(rate),
    fillOpacity = 0.75,
    label = ~map_label,
    popup = ~map_label,
    weight = 1,
    color = "black"
  ) |>
  # Give the rate units and year in the legend
  addLegend(
    pal = overall_colours,
    values = ~rate,
    title = htmltools::HTML("violent crimes<br>per 100,000<br>residents, 2012"),
    position = "bottomright"
  ) |>
  # Acknowledge the statistical and boundary sources
  addControl(
    "Crime: Statistics Bureau of Japan (CC BY)<br>Boundaries: OCHA (CC BY-IGO)",
    position = "topright"
  )
```


## Recorded homicides

The national rate was `r number(pull(filter(national_rates, crime_type == "homicides"), "rate"), accuracy = 0.1)` homicides per 100,000 residents. The highest prefecture rate was in `r pull(filter(highest, crime_type == "homicides"), "label")` and the lowest was `r pull(filter(lowest, crime_type == "homicides"), "label")`. @fig-homicides shows how rates varied across the country.
